intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of the 12th-century Khmer empire. Book a tuk-tuk from a hotel within Siem Reap's central hub to minimize travel time. Given a late Day 1 arrival, schedule this for Day 2 morning when fully rested.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda
experiences.description: Visit the stunning royal residence and the Silver Pagoda housing priceless Buddhist artifacts and a life-sized gold Buddha. Stay near the Riverside district to walk or take a short ride. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 of a Phnom Penh leg, avoiding the late-arrival Day 1 fatigue.

experiences.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Killing Fields Tour
experiences.description: A deeply moving and essential historical experience covering the Khmer Rouge era at the S-21 prison and Choeung Ek memorial. Choose a hotel in the BKK1 or Riverside area of Phnom Penh to keep transfers under 15 minutes. Best visited mid-trip when settled, not on a late-arrival day.
experiences.location: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek, Phnom Penh

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Spend two days on the pristine white-sand beaches of Koh Rong Samloem, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters and relaxing in a beachfront bungalow. Take the ferry from Sihanoukville port, and book accommodation on the island itself to avoid costly and time-consuming mainland transfers. Schedule mid-trip to allow full days on the island.

experiences.name: Siem Reap Old Market Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through Phsar Chas (Old Market) sampling local street food including fish amok, lok lak, and fresh sugarcane juice, then explore the nearby artisan shops and Pub Street cultural murals. Stay in the Old Market or Wat Bo neighborhood to walk directly to this experience without any transport cost. A perfect low-key activity for Day 2 evening after the late Day 1 arrival.
experiences.location: Old Market (Phsar Chas) District, Siem Reap

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Siem Reap Boutique Stay. After settling in, take a leisurely walk through the Old Market (Psar Chas) area to get oriented. Browse local stalls, pick up a SIM card, and exchange currency at a local money changer for better rates.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the surrounding alleyways to soak up the lively atmosphere. Visit the Night Market (Angkor Night Market) for budget souvenirs and local handicrafts. Enjoy a relaxed first evening getting acquainted with the city.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a street food stall near the hotel upon arrival (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Pub Street — affordable authentic Khmer dishes like Amok fish curry and fried rice (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: November is the start of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather (~28–32°C) with minimal rain. Perfect timing for temple visits. Keep small USD bills handy as Cambodia widely accepts USD alongside Khmer Riel.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (5:30 AM) to catch the iconic sunrise at Angkor Wat. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass (~$62 USD) at the ticket booth — the best value if you plan to visit over multiple days. Watch the sun rise over the iconic spires reflected in the lotus pond. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — visit the South Gate with its giant stone faces, the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, Baphoun Temple, and the Elephant Terrace. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$12–15 USD) for convenient transport between temples.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and relax. Visit the Angkor National Museum if energy allows (~$12 USD) for historical context, or save it for another day. Head to the Old Market area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — grab a baguette and coffee from a street vendor near Angkor Wat (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Angkor Thom — try Bai Sach Chrouk (pork and rice) or noodle soup (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Mahob Restaurant on Sivatha Street — affordable Khmer set meals (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Angkor Wat by 5:30 AM for the best sunrise spot in front of the reflecting pool. Bring a flashlight for early entry. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter temples.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 2 of the Angkor Pass to explore the jungle temples. Visit Ta Prohm (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone walls — a truly dramatic and photogenic site. Arrive early before tour groups arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Banteay Kdei and the serene Srah Srang reservoir. Then visit Pre Rup temple for panoramic views from its elevated towers. Continue to the East Mebon temple built on an artificial island.
day_by_day.evening: Back in town, explore the vibrant Kandal Village area — a hip neighborhood with indie cafes, boutique shops, and street art. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar with views of the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local Khmer porridge (Bobor) from a street stall (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch — buy fresh fruit, bread, and snacks from a roadside vendor near the temples (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Bugs Cafe (adventurous budget option) or Chamkar Vegetarian Restaurant — filling meals (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets very crowded by mid-morning. Wear sturdy shoes as temple grounds can be uneven. The Angkor Archaeological Park covers over 400 sq km — a tuk-tuk or bicycle rental (~$3–5/day) is essential for getting around efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 3 of the Angkor Pass for the outer temple circuit. Visit the stunning Banteay Srei temple (~35 km north of Siem Reap) — known as the 'Citadel of Women' for its intricate pink sandstone carvings. One of the most beautifully detailed temples in the Angkor complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Landmine Museum (free/donation) on the way back — a sobering and educational experience about Cambodia's recent history with landmines. Then visit Banteay Samre temple, a well-preserved but often overlooked gem.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at Angkor Village Theatre or Smile of Angkor (~$15–20 USD) — a cultural highlight showcasing ancient Khmer dance traditions. Book tickets in advance.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near the hotel — fresh baguette with pâté (French-Khmer fusion) and iced coffee (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Banteay Srei village — simple rice dishes (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at a restaurant near the performance venue — try Khmer BBQ (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk or negotiate a half-day tour for the Banteay Srei trip as it's further from the main complex. The Landmine Museum is a powerful reminder of Cambodia's tragic recent history — highly recommended for cultural understanding. Apsara performances usually start at 7:30 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonle Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Visit a floating village (Kampong Phluk or Chong Khneas) to witness the unique lifestyle of communities living entirely on water. Boat tours cost ~$10–15 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop in Siem Reap — a free tour showing traditional Khmer silk weaving, stone carving, and lacquerware. Great for understanding living cultural heritage and supporting local artisans. Browse the shop for affordable, quality souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Siem Reap River walk at dusk. Visit the colorful Psar Chas (Old Market) for last-minute shopping. Enjoy a traditional Khmer cooking class in the evening (~$15–20 USD) — learn to make Amok, green mango salad, and spring rolls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local market breakfast — rice soup and tea (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Floating village restaurant or packed lunch on the boat — fresh fish dishes (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner — eat what you cook! Or nearby local restaurant (~$3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Tonle Sap Lake is at its highest water level in November — ideal for boat trips. Kampong Phluk is more scenic but further; Chong Khneas is closer and cheaper. Negotiate boat prices before boarding. The cooking class is a memorable cultural experience worth the splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap early by bus to Phnom Penh (~6 hours, ~$6–10 USD via Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — the most reliable budget options). Book tickets a day in advance. Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh (~1–2 PM). Check in to a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area (~$8–15 USD/night). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (entry ~$10 USD) — stunning examples of Khmer royal architecture with gilded spires and sacred Buddhist relics.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay (Riverside Promenade) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers. Browse the riverside vendors and enjoy the cool evening breeze.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — banh mi sandwich from a street vendor (~$1 USD)
meals.lunch: Bus stop meal or packed snacks during the journey (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant — try Khmer fish amok or lok lak (beef stir-fry) with river views (~$4–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Siem Reap to Phnom Penh bus in advance, especially during peak season. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and reliability. The journey takes approximately 5.5–6.5 hours. Store luggage at the bus station if needed before check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention center (~$8 USD entry + optional audio guide $3 USD). A deeply moving and historically essential experience. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from city center, ~$6 USD entry) — the most significant memorial site of the Khmer Rouge genocide. The audio guide is excellent and included in the entry fee. A somber but profoundly important visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and decompress with a visit to the lively Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a grand Art Deco building filled with gold, clothing, and local goods. Enjoy dinner and some quiet reflection.

meals.breakfast: Local café near guesthouse — eggs, bread, and coffee (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Simple local restaurant near Tuol Sleng — rice and curry (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Friends Restaurant (social enterprise training young Cambodians in hospitality) — delicious tapas-style Khmer food (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: These sites deal with extremely heavy historical content — the Khmer Rouge genocide (1975–1979) claimed approximately 2 million lives. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees), speak quietly, and be mindful of photography. Emotionally prepare yourself. These visits are crucial for understanding modern Cambodia.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia (~$10 USD) — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture, including pieces from Angkor. Spend 2 hours exploring the beautiful terracotta building and its central garden courtyard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the French Quarter of Phnom Penh — walk past colonial-era architecture, the Post Office, and the Hotel Le Royal. Visit Wat Phnom (the founding temple of Phnom Penh, ~$1 USD donation) for panoramic city views. Browse the Russian Market (Psar Tuol Tom Poung) for affordable local goods, clothing, and handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening sunset cruise on the Mekong River (~$8–12 USD for a 1-hour cruise) — watch the city skyline glow as the sun sets. Alternatively, enjoy sundowners at a rooftop bar along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Baguette and iced coffee at a French-style Khmer café (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Russian Market food stalls — noodle soup or fried rice (~$1.50–2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant (social enterprise, traditional Khmer cuisine) — try the tarantula appetizer if feeling brave! (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is closed on Monday mornings. Bargaining is expected at the Russian Market — start at 50% of the asking price. The sunset cruise is a relaxing way to end the Phnom Penh leg of the trip. Tuk-tuks in Phnom Penh are slightly more expensive than Siem Reap — use PassApp or Grab for fair metered prices.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh early by bus or shared taxi to Sihanoukville (~4 hours, ~$6–8 USD) — Cambodia's main beach town on the Gulf of Thailand. Alternatively, take a bus to Kampot (~3 hours, ~$5–7 USD) for a more relaxed beach and river experience. Kampot is recommended for budget travelers seeking a quieter vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot (recommended). Check in to a riverside guesthouse or hammock bungalow (~$8–12 USD/night). Rent a bicycle (~$2–3 USD/day) and explore the charming French colonial town center — admire the colorful shophouses, visit the old market, and ride along the Kampot River.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset kayak or boat trip on the Kampot River (~$5–8 USD) — watch fireflies emerge after dark in the mangroves. This magical experience is unique to the Kampot area.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — local rice porridge (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Bus stop or packed snacks during transit (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Rusty Keyhole or Epic Arts Café in Kampot — affordable riverside dining with Khmer and Western options (~$4–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is strongly recommended over Sihanoukville for budget travelers — Sihanoukville has undergone significant development and has lost much of its backpacker charm. Kampot offers a relaxed, authentic atmosphere with excellent food and beautiful natural surroundings. November weather in Kampot is ideal — dry and warm.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kep — a small, charming seaside town ~25 km from Kampot (~$5–8 USD by tuk-tuk). Visit the famous Kep Crab Market for the freshest seafood in Cambodia. Explore the crumbling French colonial villas — ghostly remnants of Cambodia's pre-war golden age.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Kep Beach or take a short boat trip to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a pristine, undeveloped island with white sand beaches and crystal-clear water (~$5 USD return boat). Swim, snorkel, or simply relax in a hammock. Return to Kampot by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Cambodia — enjoy a farewell dinner along the Kampot riverside. Reflect on the journey, browse local shops for last-minute souvenirs (Kampot pepper is world-famous and makes an excellent gift), and enjoy a cold Angkor beer as the sun sets over the river.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local market — fresh fruit platter and coffee (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Kep Crab Market — fresh grilled crab with Kampot pepper sauce (a must-try! ~$6–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Rikitikitavi or Ngor's Kitchen in Kampot — excellent riverside farewell dinner (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island is best visited in the morning when it's less crowded. Bring cash as there are no ATMs on the island. Kampot pepper (both black and red) is one of the world's finest — buy directly from a farm or market for the best price (~$3–5 USD per 100g). Plan your onward transport from Kampot in advance — buses back to Phnom Penh run regularly (~$6–8 USD, 3 hours) if needed for a departure flight.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Siem Reap Boutique Stay, check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll around the hotel neighborhood. Explore the nearby Pub Street area and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) to get your bearings and pick up a local SIM card.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Angkor Night Market for a relaxed first evening — browse local handicrafts, silk scarves, and souvenirs. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a nearby cultural venue for an immersive welcome to Khmer culture.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival — try a simple bowl of Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) at a local eatery for around $3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant near Pub Street — a mid-range Khmer restaurant offering traditional dishes like Amok fish curry and lok lak beef, averaging $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: November is the tail end of the rainy season in Cambodia — expect mostly dry and pleasant weather around 25–30°C. Keep an umbrella handy just in case. Exchange some USD to Khmer Riel for small purchases; USD is widely accepted.

day_by_day.morning: Early sunrise visit to Angkor Wat (the world's largest religious monument). Arrive by 5:30 AM to witness the iconic sunrise reflection over the moat. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs depicting Hindu mythology and the Churning of the Ocean of Milk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Angkor Archaeological Park — visit Angkor Thom (the last great capital of the Khmer Empire), the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Hire a licensed local guide ($25–35) for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit the Cambodian Cultural Village for a brief cultural overview, then enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the town.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel or grab a baguette and coffee from a street stall near Angkor (French colonial influence is strong — $2–3)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Angkor Thom — try the Khmer set lunch at Blue Pumpkin Angkor or a nearby local spot for $6–10
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak, a celebrated fine-casual Khmer restaurant offering a contemporary tasting menu of local ingredients — $25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) at the ticket office the evening before or early morning — this covers Days 2, 3, and 4. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and comfortable walking shoes. The temples involve significant walking and climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ta Prohm Temple — famously left partially unrestored with giant silk-cotton tree roots engulfing the stone structures (the 'Tomb Raider temple'). Arrive early to beat the crowds. Then visit Banteay Kdei and the serene Srah Srang reservoir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Banteay Srei Temple (about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap) — considered the 'Jewel of Khmer Art' for its intricate pink sandstone carvings. On the way back, stop at the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's painful history with unexploded ordnance and ongoing demining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's vibrant Pub Street and surrounding alleys. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage at one of the many reputable spas (60-minute traditional massage $10–15) before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel (if included) or at a local café — try a Khmer breakfast of rice porridge (Bobor) with ginger and egg at a local market stall ($2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch or eat at a local family restaurant near Banteay Srei — simple Khmer dishes like fried rice or noodles for $4–6
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training disadvantaged youth in hospitality. Mid-range pricing ($8–12) with excellent Khmer and Western fusion dishes

day_by_day.notes: Rent a tuk-tuk for the full day (approximately $15–20) for comfortable temple hopping. The Landmine Museum is sobering but highly educational — a must for understanding modern Cambodian history.

day_by_day.morning: Use the final day of the Angkor Pass to visit the remote and less-crowded temples of the Grand Circuit — Preah Khan (a vast monastic complex), Neak Pean (a unique island temple in a reservoir), and Ta Som with its beautiful east gopura engulfed by a fig tree.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the East Mebon Temple and Pre Rup (a late 10th-century state temple with great views from the top). Spend the late afternoon at the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for a comprehensive overview of Khmer civilization, art, and the Angkor period ($12 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a shadow puppet (Sbek Thom) performance or a traditional Apsara dance show at Smile of Angkor or Apsara Theatre — a culturally rich evening experience ($15–25 with dinner option).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a French-Khmer bakery breakfast near the Old Market — croissant, coffee, and tropical fruit ($4–6)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near the Grand Circuit temples — try Khmer curry with rice ($5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner included at the Apsara dance show venue, or dine at Sugar Palm Restaurant for authentic home-style Khmer cooking ($10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the last day of the Angkor Pass. The Grand Circuit temples are less visited and offer a more peaceful atmosphere. Pre Rup at late afternoon offers beautiful golden-hour lighting for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus or private transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours by road, $10–15 by bus or $60–80 by private taxi). Alternatively, take a 45-minute domestic flight ($50–80) to save time. Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel near the riverside (Sisowath Quay area). Visit the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda — the official royal residence featuring stunning Khmer architecture and a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles ($10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the scenic Tonle Sap and Mekong riverside promenade. Watch the sunset over the confluence of the rivers from the waterfront. Explore the lively FCC (Foreign Correspondents' Club) area for evening drinks.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick stop at a local market before departure from Siem Reap
meals.lunch: Lunch stop on the road or at a roadside restaurant en route to Phnom Penh — local Khmer dishes for $4–7
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including regional specialties. Mid-range pricing ($12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Giant Ibis bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh is highly recommended for safety and comfort ($15). Book tickets in advance. Phnom Penh accommodation near the riverside (Sisowath Quay) is ideal for walkability.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. A deeply moving and essential experience for understanding Cambodia's tragic recent history ($3 entry, audio guide available).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day trip to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields), approximately 15 km from the city center. The memorial stupa and audio tour provide a profound and respectful commemoration of the victims ($6 entry with audio guide). Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia for Khmer art and artifacts ($10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a striking Art Deco building housing jewelry, clothing, and local goods. Enjoy a relaxed evening along the riverside with street food and local life.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverside café in Phnom Penh — fresh baguette, eggs, and iced coffee ($4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch after the Killing Fields visit — a quiet café near the National Museum or a local Khmer restaurant for $5–8
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends the Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — another beloved social enterprise restaurant with a diverse menu of tapas-style Cambodian dishes ($10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. Dress respectfully. These sites are critical for understanding Cambodia's history and honoring the memory of victims. Consider hiring a local guide for deeper context ($10–15).

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name, surrounded by lush gardens and resident monkeys. Then explore the Independence Monument and stroll through the tree-lined boulevards of the French colonial quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Take an afternoon bus or taxi from Phnom Penh to Kampot (approximately 3 hours, $8–12 by bus). Check into a mid-range guesthouse along the Kampot River. Explore the charming, laid-back riverside town with its French colonial architecture and pepper plantations.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cruise on the Kampot River on a local boat ($5–8 per person). Watch fireflies light up the mangroves as darkness falls — a magical Kampot experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local Phnom Penh café breakfast — rice porridge, fried dough sticks (Chakquai), and iced coffee ($3–5)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch before departure at a local Phnom Penh restaurant or on the road
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi or Epic Arts Café in Kampot — riverside dining with Khmer and international options in a relaxed atmosphere ($8–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is one of Cambodia's most charming small towns — famous for its world-renowned Kampot pepper, colonial architecture, and easy-going vibe. November is a great time to visit as the weather is dry and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a Kampot pepper farm for a guided tour — learn about the cultivation and processing of the world-famous Kampot pepper (red, black, and white varieties). Many farms offer free or low-cost tours ($5–10). Then explore the Kampot Old Town on foot or by bicycle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Kep — a sleepy former French colonial beach resort town 25 km from Kampot (tuk-tuk $8–12 return). Visit the famous Kep Crab Market and relax on Kep Beach. Explore the ruins of the old French villas and the beautiful Kep National Park trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for the evening. Enjoy a sunset drink at a riverside bar. Experience the vibrant but relaxed Kampot nightlife along the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Kampot riverside café — fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and Khmer coffee ($4–6)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Kep Crab Market — fresh steamed crab with Kampot pepper sauce, a bucket of clams, and grilled seafood ($10–15 per person — a must-do culinary experience)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Baraka or The Rusty Keyhole in Kampot — excellent mid-range restaurants with Khmer and international menus ($8–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Kep Crab Market is one of the great culinary experiences in Southeast Asia — do not miss it. Rent a bicycle in Kampot for easy and fun local exploration ($2–3/day). Kep Beach is small but pleasant for a swim.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Bokor Hill Station (Preah Monivong National Park) — a dramatic plateau 1,075 meters above sea level with stunning views over the Gulf of Thailand. Explore the eerie abandoned French colonial resort, the old casino, and the hilltop Buddhist pagoda. Rent a motorbike or hire a tuk-tuk for the journey ($15–20 round trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Kampot to Sihanoukville (approximately 1.5–2 hours, $5–8 by minibus) and take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (approximately 45 minutes, $25–30 return). Check into a beachside bungalow or guesthouse on Saracen Bay — one of Cambodia's most beautiful beaches with calm turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the pristine beach as the sun sets. Enjoy bioluminescent plankton in the water after dark — a spectacular natural phenomenon best seen by wading or swimming in the shallows.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Kampot before the Bokor trip — simple guesthouse breakfast or local market food ($3–5)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kampot or Sihanoukville before the ferry — local Khmer restaurant ($5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Koh Rong Samloem — fresh grilled fish, seafood curry, and tropical cocktails on the beach ($10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bokor Hill Station is often misty and atmospheric — bring a light jacket. Koh Rong Samloem is far less developed and more peaceful than the main Koh Rong island — ideal for a balanced beach experience. Book island accommodation in advance as options are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise swim on Saracen Bay. Snorkel along the coral reef just offshore (snorkel gear rental $5). Take a guided kayak tour around the island's mangroves and hidden beaches (half-day tour $15–20).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the afternoon ferry back to Sihanoukville. Depending on your departure flight, either head directly to Phnom Penh International Airport (3.5–4 hours) or spend a few final hours in Sihanoukville. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping — Kampot pepper, silk scarves, and Khmer silverware make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia with memories of ancient temples, rich history, vibrant culture, and stunning coastal beauty. If time permits before departure, enjoy a final Khmer meal at a restaurant near the airport.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the island — tropical fruit platter, eggs, and fresh coconut at a beachfront café ($5–7)
meals.lunch: Lunch on the ferry or in Sihanoukville — local seafood or Khmer noodles ($5–8)
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a restaurant near Phnom Penh airport or a farewell meal in Sihanoukville — Khmer amok, lok lak, and a Chang beer to toast the journey ($10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules carefully — ferries from Koh Rong Samloem to Sihanoukville run a few times daily. Allow at least 4–5 hours from the ferry port to Phnom Penh airport for international departures. Cambodia's beauty, warmth, and resilience will leave a lasting impression.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged with your boutique hotel's luxury vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Siem Reap Boutique Stay. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the charming French Quarter and along the Siem Reap River promenade to ease into the destination.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the city skyline, followed by a curated introduction to Khmer culture with a private Apsara dance performance dinner at a premium heritage restaurant.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant — award-winning modern Khmer cuisine in an elegant garden setting, paired with Cambodian craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light as jet lag may be a factor. Confirm Apsara dinner show reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private sunrise tour of Angkor Wat — arrive before 5:30 AM to witness the iconic reflection of the temple in the lotus pond. Your private expert guide will provide in-depth historical and architectural commentary as the temple comes to life in golden light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the walled city of Angkor Thom, including the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by your hotel chef in the shade of the ancient ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a traditional Khmer herbal bath and 90-minute signature massage at the hotel spa. Dinner at a fine dining restaurant in Siem Reap's upscale dining district.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast box prepared by the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic lunch among the Angkor Thom ruins
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak — celebrated tasting menu of refined Cambodian cuisine using local seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Bring sunscreen, insect repellent, and a hat. Temple dress code requires covered shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Ta Prohm — the mystical jungle temple famously engulfed by ancient strangler fig and silk-cotton trees. Explore in the early hours before crowds arrive. Continue to Preah Khan, a sprawling 12th-century monastic complex largely unrestored and deeply atmospheric.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum for a premium guided experience through seven galleries showcasing Khmer civilization, sculpture, and the history of the Angkor Empire. Followed by a private workshop on traditional Khmer silk weaving at a local artisan cooperative.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a private boat cruise along the Tonlé Sap Lake, watching the sun dip below the horizon over Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Return to the hotel for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Private lunch at a curated local restaurant near the museum — traditional fish amok and green mango salad
meals.dinner: The Sugar Palm — intimate Khmer restaurant celebrated for authentic family recipes and a refined atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap boat cruise should be booked in advance. November is a great time to visit as water levels are high after the rainy season.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the remote and rarely visited Beng Mealea Temple — a sprawling 12th-century ruin largely reclaimed by jungle, offering an adventurous and deeply immersive archaeological experience without the crowds. Private vehicle and expert guide included.
day_by_day.afternoon: En route back, stop at a traditional Cambodian village for a private cultural immersion experience — meet local artisans, observe traditional pottery making, and enjoy a cooking demonstration of rural Khmer cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Enjoy a private rooftop dinner under the stars with a curated Cambodian and French fusion tasting menu, honoring the country's colonial culinary heritage.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional home-cooked Khmer meal hosted by a local family in the village
meals.dinner: Private rooftop dining experience at the hotel or a luxury partner restaurant — Champagne and Khmer-French fusion tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Beng Mealea is approximately 68 km from Siem Reap (about 1.5 hours). Wear sturdy footwear as the terrain is uneven. An early start is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 45 minutes) for a dramatic aerial view of the Cambodian landscape and Mekong River delta. Check in to a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided visit to the Royal Palace and the stunning Silver Pagoda, home to a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds. Continue to the National Museum of Cambodia for an extensive collection of Khmer art and antiquities.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset river cruise on the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence aboard a private luxury boat with Champagne and canapés. Dinner at one of Phnom Penh's premier fine dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the Siem Reap hotel before helicopter transfer
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside café in Phnom Penh — fresh spring rolls and Cambodian noodle soup
meals.dinner: Topaz Restaurant — Phnom Penh's iconic fine dining institution with French and Cambodian cuisine and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter transfers must be booked well in advance. Dress modestly for Royal Palace visit — no bare shoulders or shorts. Keep passport handy for hotel check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Guided visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — a deeply moving and historically essential experience that provides crucial context for understanding Cambodia's modern history. Private guide with expert historical knowledge recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) and the Central Market for premium Cambodian handicrafts, silk scarves, silver jewelry, and gemstones. Private shopping concierge available to identify authentic artisan pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private classical Khmer dance performance at a cultural center, followed by dinner at a celebrated restaurant along the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Phnom Penh luxury hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Romdeng — social enterprise restaurant in a colonial villa serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including regional specialties
meals.dinner: Bistrot Langka — elegant French-Cambodian bistro with a sophisticated wine cellar and seasonal menu

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy. Allow time for reflection. Photography is permitted in most areas but approach with deep respect.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Phnom Penh to Kep (approximately 3 hours by luxury vehicle) — a charming coastal town known for its French colonial villas, pristine beaches, and legendary crab market. Check in to a premium boutique resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kep National Park with a private nature guide — hike through lush forest trails with panoramic views of the Gulf of Thailand and offshore islands. Visit the iconic Crab Market to select fresh live crab for your evening meal.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset on the beach at Kep's tranquil shoreline, followed by a private beachside dinner featuring your freshly selected crab prepared in Kampot pepper sauce — a local culinary icon.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Phnom Penh hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch en route or at a stop in Kampot town — fresh local produce and artisan bread
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner at the resort — Kep crab with Kampot pepper, grilled seafood, and Cambodian tropical fruit dessert

day_by_day.notes: Kep is a small, peaceful town — ideal for unwinding after the intensity of Phnom Penh. Kampot pepper is a world-renowned delicacy; purchase some to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat excursion to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — one of Cambodia's most pristine and undeveloped islands with white sandy beaches and crystal-clear waters. Snorkeling equipment provided. Enjoy the island in the early morning before day visitors arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kep. Visit a working Kampot pepper farm for a private guided tour and tasting — learn about the cultivation of one of the world's most prized peppers. Browse the farm's premium pepper selection for gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the beach at the resort, followed by a spa treatment using traditional Khmer botanicals. Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before boat departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood barbecue on Rabbit Island beach — grilled fish, prawns, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Knai Bang Chatt Resort Restaurant — refined Cambodian coastal cuisine with stunning sunset views over the Gulf of Thailand

day_by_day.notes: November weather in Kep is typically dry and pleasant — ideal for beach and island activities. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Book the pepper farm tour in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Kep to Sihanoukville (approximately 2.5 hours) and onwards by speedboat to Koh Rong Samloem — Cambodia's most exclusive and pristine island retreat. Check in to a luxury overwater or beachfront villa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island's stunning Saracen Bay — swim in turquoise waters, kayak through mangroves, or simply relax on the powder-white beach. Optional private snorkeling tour of the surrounding coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the extraordinary bioluminescent plankton phenomenon in the bay after dark — a magical natural light show visible in the warm coastal waters. Followed by a private candlelit beach dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Kep resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the island resort upon arrival — fresh coconut, tropical salads, and grilled reef fish
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beach dinner at the water's edge — lobster, grilled seafood platter, and Cambodian desserts with sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rong Samloem has limited connectivity — embrace the digital detox. The bioluminescent plankton is best seen on moonless nights; check lunar calendar in advance. Bring cash as ATMs are unavailable on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach — a peaceful farewell to Cambodia's coastline. Enjoy a slow morning with a spa treatment, swim, or simply relax in your villa. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Speedboat transfer back to Sihanoukville, then private luxury vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport or back to Siem Reap depending on departure flight logistics. En route, stop for a final Cambodian lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia. If flight is late evening, enjoy a final cocktail and light dinner at the airport lounge or a nearby luxury hotel day room.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte breakfast at the island resort — tropical fruit, eggs benedict, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Final Cambodian lunch at a riverside restaurant in Sihanoukville or Phnom Penh — amok curry, lok lak beef, and fresh sugarcane juice
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or hotel day room dinner depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer and flight details the evening before. Allow extra time for speedboat and road transfers — approximately 4–5 hours total from island to airport. Consider purchasing Kampot pepper, silk scarves, and Cambodian gemstones as premium souvenirs.
